functions.name: addEntraIdApplication
functions.description: Adds a Microsoft Entra ID application registration resource to the application model.
functions.remarks:
Provisions an application and service principal through Microsoft Graph Bicep. Requires Azure provisioning
configuration and permission to create registrations in the subscription's tenant.
Reference the registration from a workload to inject authentication configuration as environment variables.
To reference an existing registration without Azure or Graph access, use addExistingEntraIdApplication.
Workloads must configure their own authentication library.

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The name of the resource.

functions.name: addExistingEntraIdApplication
functions.description: References an existing registration without enabling Azure provisioning or querying Microsoft Graph.
functions.remarks: Literal IDs are validated immediately; parameter values are validated at startup. Other Azure resources retain their provisioning setup.
functions.signature: addExistingEntraIdApplication(name: string, tenantId: string | ParameterResource, clientId: string | ParameterResource): EntraIdApplicationResource

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The resource name.

parameters.name: tenantId
parameters.description: The registration's home tenant GUID or domain, as a literal or parameter. Sign-in keywords are not home tenant IDs.

parameters.name: clientId
parameters.description: The registration's application client GUID, as a literal or parameter.

functions.name: asExistingApplication
functions.description: References an existing registration without undoing the Azure provisioning setup enabled when this resource was added.
functions.remarks:
The registration itself is not provisioned or queried. Deployment can still require Azure authentication and configuration.
Use addExistingEntraIdApplication instead for a configuration-only AppHost without Azure setup.
Throws before changing the resource if registration-only configuration was already applied.
functions.signature: asExistingApplication(tenantId: string | ParameterResource, clientId: string | ParameterResource): EntraIdApplicationResource

parameters.name: tenantId
parameters.description: The registration's home tenant GUID or domain, as a literal or parameter.

parameters.name: clientId
parameters.description: The registration's application client GUID, as a literal or parameter.

functions.name: getScopeUri
functions.description: Gets an expression for the full URI of one of this registration's scopes, such as api://{clientId}/access_as_user.
functions.remarks: Clients request the full URI as the token scope. Throws when the registration has no such scope, or is an existing registration without an application ID URI.
functions.returns: An expression that resolves when the registration's application ID URI is known.

parameters.name: scopeName
parameters.description: The name of a scope added with withScope.

functions.name: publishWithAppRoleAssignment
functions.description: Publishes explicit application-role assignments to a managed identity or a compute resource's managed identity.
functions.remarks:
Has no effect during local run. Existing registrations are not modified. No caller registration or federation is created.
Requires Graph AppRoleAssignment.ReadWrite.All and Application.Read.All (or higher application-read permission), administrator
consent and, for delegated deployment, a supported Entra directory role. Removing a call does not revoke a deployed grant.
functions.signature: publishWithAppRoleAssignment(identity: AzureUserAssignedIdentityResource | IComputeResource, roleValues: string[]): EntraIdApplicationResource

parameters.name: identity
parameters.description: The user-assigned identity or compute resource receiving the roles.

parameters.name: roleValues
parameters.description: Enabled role values declared on this API that allow Application members.

functions.name: publishWithFederatedManagedIdentityCredential
functions.description: Publishes managed identity federation trust for a registration created by Aspire.
functions.remarks:
Not used during local run. Throws for existing registrations. A selected compute resource must reference this registration.
With an explicit identity, each consumer must use that identity. Only Azure public, US Government and China clouds are supported.

parameters.name: identity
parameters.description: A compute resource whose identity to trust, an explicit user-assigned identity, or no value to trust every consumer's own identity.

functions.name: runWithLocalDeveloperCertificateCredential
functions.description: Creates and provisions a short-lived certificate credential for local development.
functions.remarks:
Each application gets a dedicated certificate in the AppHost's local store. Certificates last two days;
on a subsequent run, a certificate with one day or less remaining is replaced by overwriting its PFX file.
Only the public certificate is provisioned in Entra. Referencing applications receive the private
credential as a secret `Base64EncodedValue` in Microsoft.Identity.Web's `ClientCredentials` configuration.
Aspire replaces the registration's entire `keyCredentials` collection with the selected certificate.
Existing certificate credentials are not retained, so older sessions must restart after renewal.
Development and production must use separate Entra registrations. Never register developer certificates
on a production application. Different resource groups do not isolate tenant-scoped registrations:
use distinct registration names or tenant-resource suffixes. This method does not provision or emit a credential when publishing;
omitting a credential from publish does not revoke a key previously registered against the same application.
In either mode, this configuration prevents conversion to an existing registration with `AsExistingApplication`.
Renewal is checked at AppHost startup, not in the background. Restart long-running development sessions
before the certificate expires. Use `PublishWithFederatedManagedIdentityCredential` for deployed workloads.

functions.name: withAdminConsent
functions.description: Grants tenant-wide consent to delegated permissions that this registration declared for another registration in the AppHost.
functions.remarks:
This creates a delegated permission grant for all users (`consentType: AllPrincipals`) from this registration to
`api`, so nobody is prompted to consent. The identity that deploys needs a directory role such as
Privileged Role Administrator, Cloud Application Administrator or Application Administrator, or a privileged
Microsoft Graph permission such as `DelegatedPermissionGrant.ReadWrite.All`. Deployment fails without it.
See .
A grant is neither a declaration nor a pre-authorization. Throws for an existing caller; grant its consent manually
in the Microsoft Entra admin center. A created caller may consent to an existing API.
The grant is declared in full: it is set to exactly the scopes passed to `WithAdminConsent` for this registration and
`api`. A scope that was granted to the pair outside Aspire, or that is removed from the calls while others remain,
is revoked by the next deployment. When no call remains for the pair, nothing is sent and the existing grant stays.

parameters.name: api
parameters.description: The registration that exposes the scopes.

parameters.name: scopeNames
parameters.description: The names of scopes already declared with `WithApiPermissions`.

functions.name: withAllowWebApiToBeAuthorizedByACL
functions.description: Enables ACL-based authorization for daemon-to-API scenarios.

functions.name: withApiPermissions
functions.description: Declares that this registration requires delegated permissions to scopes of another registration in the AppHost.

parameters.name: api
parameters.description: The registration that exposes the scopes.

parameters.name: scopeNames
parameters.description: The names of the scopes, added with `WithScope` to `api`.

functions.name: withApplicationIdUri
functions.description: Exposes the registration as an API identified by an application ID URI.

parameters.name: applicationIdUri
parameters.description: A custom URI, such as api://contoso-orders or https://contoso.onmicrosoft.com/orders. Omit to use the default api://{clientId}.

functions.name: withApplicationOwners
functions.description: Appends an application owner supplied as a literal directory object GUID or a parameter.
functions.remarks: Call repeatedly for multiple owners. Existing owners are not removed. Throws for existing registrations; configure their owners manually.

parameters.name: ownerObjectId
parameters.description: The directory object ID of a user or service principal.

functions.name: withAppRole
functions.description: Declares an application role on a registration created by Aspire.
functions.remarks:
Application roles are separate from delegated scopes and from Azure RBAC roles. This only declares the role; it does not assign it or grant consent.
Role IDs stay the same across deployments, and changing a role's value or ID creates a different role. Whenever at least one role is declared,
the complete appRoles collection is sent, so include every role to keep. Microsoft Graph rejects deleting an enabled role.
Existing registrations are never modified, so this throws for registrations created with addExistingEntraIdApplication.
functions.signature: withAppRole(value: string, displayName: string, description: string, allowedMemberTypes?: string[], id?: string, isEnabled?: boolean): EntraIdApplicationResource

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The value emitted in the roles claim, for example Admin. It must be unique for the application, at most 120 characters, must not start with a period, and may contain only ASCII letters, digits and the punctuation that Microsoft Graph allows.

parameters.name: displayName
parameters.description: The display name shown in the Microsoft Entra admin center.

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: The description shown in assignment and consent experiences.

parameters.name: allowedMemberTypes
parameters.description: The member types the role can be assigned to, passed through to Microsoft Graph (for example User or Application). Defaults to User.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: An optional role GUID. When omitted, a stable ID is derived from the registration's resource name and value.

parameters.name: isEnabled
parameters.description: Whether the role is enabled. Defaults to true. To retire a role, deploy it with false and leave it declared; disabling is not access revocation because existing assignments still receive the role in tokens.

functions.name: withAudience
functions.description: Adds an accepted audience for this application.
functions.remarks: Configures consumer token validation only. It does not change application ID URIs on created or existing registrations.

parameters.name: audience
parameters.description: The audience value (e.g., `api://<client-id>`).

functions.name: withCertificateDistinguishedName
functions.description: Adds a certificate credential from the certificate store by distinguished name.

parameters.name: storePath
parameters.description: The certificate store path (e.g., `"CurrentUser/My"`).

parameters.name: distinguishedName
parameters.description: The certificate distinguished name (e.g., `"CN=MyCert"`).

functions.name: withCertificateFromFile
functions.description: Appends a certificate file credential. The file path is on the consuming resource, not the AppHost.
functions.remarks: The password must be marked secret and remains a deferred parameter. File credentials are not recommended for production.

parameters.name: filePath

parameters.name: password
parameters.description: An optional secret parameter for a password-protected certificate.

functions.name: withCertificateFromKeyVault
functions.description: Adds a certificate credential using a vault URL or Key Vault resource.
functions.remarks: The latest certificate version is used. Resource-backed vaults grant consumers the Key Vault Certificate User role by default.
functions.signature: withCertificateFromKeyVault(keyVaultUrl: string | AzureKeyVaultResource, certificateName: string): EntraIdApplicationResource

parameters.name: keyVaultUrl
parameters.description: The vault URL or Key Vault resource containing the certificate.

parameters.name: certificateName
parameters.description: The name of the certificate in Key Vault.

functions.name: withCertificateThumbprint
functions.description: Adds a certificate credential from the certificate store by thumbprint.

parameters.name: storePath
parameters.description: The certificate store path (e.g., `"CurrentUser/My"`).

parameters.name: thumbprint
parameters.description: The certificate thumbprint.

functions.name: withClientCapability
functions.description: Adds a client capability (e.g., `"cp1"` for Continuous Access Evaluation).

parameters.name: capability
parameters.description: The capability identifier.

functions.name: withClientSecret
functions.description: Adds a client secret credential to this Entra ID application.
functions.remarks:
This adds an entry to the `ClientCredentials` array in the Microsoft.Identity.Web
configuration with `SourceType` set to `"ClientSecret"`.

parameters.name: clientSecret
parameters.description: A secret parameter containing the client secret.

functions.name: withEntraIdReference
functions.description: Injects Entra ID authentication configuration into a consuming resource and sets the prefix of its DownstreamApis entries.
functions.remarks:
Behaves like withReference with the registration, which is enough for most references. Use this method when a resource references several registrations
that declare permissions to the same API: give all but one of them their own downstreamApisPrefix, or the model is rejected.
functions.signature: withEntraIdReference(source: EntraIdApplicationResource, connectionName?: string, downstreamApisPrefix?: string): IResourceWithEnvironment

parameters.name: source
parameters.description: The Entra ID application resource to reference.

parameters.name: connectionName
parameters.description: The environment variable prefix. Defaults to AzureAd for .NET program resources and the registration's name otherwise.

parameters.name: downstreamApisPrefix
parameters.description: The configuration prefix of the DownstreamApis entries. Defaults to DownstreamApis.

functions.name: withExternalApiAdminConsent
functions.description: Grants tenant-wide consent to permissions that this registration declared for an API that is not an Aspire resource.
functions.remarks:
A delegated permission becomes a delegated permission grant for all users. An application permission becomes an app role assignment
to this registration's service principal. The deploying identity needs a directory role or Microsoft Graph permission that allows consent, and deployment fails without it.
Application permissions to broad scopes such as Directory.Read.All give the application access to the whole tenant, so grant only what the application needs.
Throws when a permission was not declared first or the caller is an existing registration. Grant consent for existing registrations manually.
Consent is not additive. The delegated grant is declared in full: it is set to exactly the delegated permissions passed to withExternalApiAdminConsent
for this registration and API, so a permission granted to the pair outside Aspire, or removed from the calls while others remain, is revoked by the next deployment.
When no delegated call remains for the pair, nothing is sent and the existing grant stays. Each application permission is a separate app role assignment:
Aspire creates it but does not delete it when its consent is removed from the AppHost, so remove it in the Microsoft Entra admin center.
functions.signature: withExternalApiAdminConsent(api: EntraIdWellKnownApi | EntraIdCustomApi, permissions: EntraIdExternalApiPermission[]): EntraIdApplicationResource

parameters.name: api
parameters.description: A well-known API, or an API identified by its application ID and application ID URI.

parameters.name: permissions
parameters.description: Permissions already declared with withExternalApiPermissions.

functions.name: withExternalApiPermissions
functions.description: Declares permissions to a Microsoft first-party or other API that is not an Aspire resource, such as Microsoft Graph.
functions.signature: withExternalApiPermissions(api: EntraIdWellKnownApi | EntraIdCustomApi, permissions: EntraIdExternalApiPermission[]): EntraIdApplicationResource

parameters.name: api
parameters.description: A well-known API, or an API identified by its application ID and application ID URI.

parameters.name: permissions
parameters.description: The permissions to declare. Each is delegated unless its type is Application.

functions.name: withExtraQueryParameter
functions.description: Adds an extra query parameter to send to the identity provider.

parameters.name: key
parameters.description: The query parameter key.

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: The query parameter value.

functions.name: withFederatedManagedIdentityCredential
functions.description: Configures a pre-existing managed identity trust for token acquisition, without provisioning or assigning an identity.
functions.remarks: Applies in run and publish modes. This only emits consumer configuration; it does not create federation trust.

parameters.name: managedIdentityClientId
parameters.description: The client GUID of a user-assigned managed identity that the registration already trusts.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: Optional token exchange settings.

functions.name: withIdTokenIssuance
functions.description: Enables ID-token issuance through implicit and hybrid flows for a registration created by Aspire.

functions.name: withInstance
functions.description: Configures the Entra ID instance URL. Defaults to `https://login.microsoftonline.com/`.

parameters.name: instance
parameters.description: The Entra ID instance URL, such as `https://login.microsoftonline.us/` for Azure Government or `https://contoso.ciamlogin.com/` for an external tenant.

functions.name: withOwners
functions.description: Appends an owner to both the application registration and service principal.
functions.remarks: Owners can manage the registration. Call repeatedly for multiple owners. Throws for existing registrations; configure their owners manually.

parameters.name: ownerObjectId
parameters.description: The directory object GUID of a user or service principal, as a literal or parameter.

functions.name: withPreAuthorizedApplication
functions.description: Pre-authorizes a client application to request some of this registration's scopes without any consent prompt.
functions.remarks:
Pre-authorization is separate from the client's declaration of the permission (`WithApiPermissions`)
and from consent (`WithAdminConsent`).
It lets a trusted client skip the consent prompt, which is intended for first-party clients of the same organization.
Aspire deploys each registration as its own module. Pre-authorization makes this registration wait for the client's ID, while
the client's declaration waits for this registration's ID, so two registrations cannot use both. Use a declaration with
`WithAdminConsent` on the client, or pre-authorization alone. Throws if this API registration is existing;
configure its pre-authorized clients manually. An existing client can still be pre-authorized by a registration Aspire creates.

parameters.name: client
parameters.description: The client application to pre-authorize.

parameters.name: scopeNames
parameters.description: The names of the scopes, added with `WithScope`, that the client may request.

functions.name: withRedirectUris
functions.description: Appends web redirect URIs supplied as a literal, a parameter, or an endpoint.
functions.signature: withRedirectUris(redirectUri: string | ParameterResource | EndpointReference, callbackPaths?: string[]): EntraIdApplicationResource

parameters.name: redirectUri
parameters.description: A full URI, a parameter containing comma-separated full URIs, or an endpoint. With callback paths, a parameter supplies a host instead.

parameters.name: callbackPaths
parameters.description: Callback paths starting with '/'. Required for an endpoint; with a host parameter, produces HTTPS URIs. Omit for full URIs.

functions.name: withScope
functions.description: Exposes a delegated permission scope that clients can request to call this registration as an API.
functions.remarks:
Scopes are declared explicitly. Unless an application ID URI is set with withApplicationIdUri, the registration uses api://{clientId}.
The scope's ID stays the same across deployments. Microsoft Graph does not let a deployment remove an enabled scope or change its name:
to retire a scope, deploy it with isEnabled set to false and remove it in a later deployment.
For an existing registration the scope is configuration only, which lets callers declare permissions to it. Set its id to the ID the registration defines.
functions.signature: withScope(name: string, description: string, options?: EntraIdScopeOptions): EntraIdApplicationResource

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The scope's name, which appears in the token's scp claim, such as access_as_user.

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: What the scope allows, shown on the consent page.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: Optional settings for the scope.

functions.name: withSendX5C
functions.description: Sends the `x5c` claim (the public key of the certificate) with token requests.
functions.remarks:
Sending `x5c` enables certificate rollover without redeploying the application. It only applies
to certificate-based credentials and increases the size of each token request, so it is opt-in.

functions.name: withServicePrincipalOwners
functions.description: Appends a service principal owner supplied as a literal directory object GUID or a parameter.
functions.remarks: Service principal ownership is independent of application ownership. Throws for existing registrations; configure their owners manually.

parameters.name: ownerObjectId
parameters.description: The directory object ID of a user or service principal.

functions.name: withSignedAssertionFile
functions.description: Appends a signed assertion file credential, such as an AKS workload identity token.

parameters.name: filePath
parameters.description: The token file path on the consumer. Omit to use the consumer's AZURE_FEDERATED_TOKEN_FILE setting.

functions.name: withSignInAudience
functions.description: Configures which accounts can sign in to this application.
functions.remarks:
The audience must match the registration's supported account types. The default uses the home tenant as TenantId.
Other audiences use organizations, common, or consumers as TenantId and also emit AppHomeTenantId.
Also configures supported account types on registrations created by Aspire. For existing registrations, configures consumers only.
Validate the tenant ID (tid) claim before allowing access to tenant-specific data.
See https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity-platform/claims-validation.

parameters.name: signInAudience
parameters.description: The accounts that can sign in. It must match the "Supported account types" setting of the app registration.

handleTypes.name: EntraIdApplicationResource
handleTypes.description: A resource that represents a Microsoft Entra ID application registration.
handleTypes.remarks:
Entra ID application registrations define the identity configuration for services
in a distributed application. Each application registration includes a tenant ID,
client ID, and optionally client credentials and API scopes.
Aspire creates new registrations using a resource-group-scoped Microsoft Graph Bicep deployment.
Use `AddExistingEntraIdApplication` to reference an existing registration without deploying infrastructure.
Registration-only builder APIs throw on existing references. Converting a resource with
`AsExistingApplication` also throws if registration-only configuration was already applied.
Consumer configuration and explicit metadata describing existing API URIs and scopes remain supported.
References to this resource inject configuration as environment variables.
.NET program references default to names such as `AzureAd__TenantId` and `AzureAd__ClientId`,
compatible with Microsoft.Identity.Web. Other references default to an uppercase resource-name prefix
and a single underscore separator, and can configure their own prefix and separator.
The properties align with `MicrosoftEntraApplicationOptions` from
`Microsoft.Identity.Abstractions`.

capabilities.name: withCertificateThumbprint

parameters.name: storePath

parameters.name: thumbprint

parameters.name: capability

capabilities.name: withClientSecret
capabilities.description: Adds a client secret credential to this Entra ID application.
capabilities.remarks:
This adds an entry to the `ClientCredentials` array in the Microsoft.Identity.Web
configuration with `SourceType` set to `"ClientSecret"`.

parameters.name: clientSecret
parameters.description: A secret parameter containing the client secret.

capabilities.name: withExternalApiAdminConsent
capabilities.description: Grants tenant-wide consent to permissions that this registration declared for an API that is not an Aspire resource.
capabilities.remarks:
A delegated permission becomes a delegated permission grant for all users. An application permission becomes an app role assignment
to this registration's service principal. The deploying identity needs a directory role or Microsoft Graph permission that allows consent, and deployment fails without it.
Application permissions to broad scopes such as Directory.Read.All give the application access to the whole tenant, so grant only what the application needs.
Throws when a permission was not declared first or the caller is an existing registration. Grant consent for existing registrations manually.
Consent is not additive. The delegated grant is declared in full: it is set to exactly the delegated permissions passed to withExternalApiAdminConsent
for this registration and API, so a permission granted to the pair outside Aspire, or removed from the calls while others remain, is revoked by the next deployment.
When no delegated call remains for the pair, nothing is sent and the existing grant stays. Each application permission is a separate app role assignment:
Aspire creates it but does not delete it when its consent is removed from the AppHost, so remove it in the Microsoft Entra admin center.
capabilities.signature: withExternalApiAdminConsent(api: EntraIdWellKnownApi | EntraIdCustomApi, permissions: EntraIdExternalApiPermission[]): EntraIdApplicationResource

parameters.name: api
parameters.description: A well-known API, or an API identified by its application ID and application ID URI.

parameters.name: permissions
parameters.description: Permissions already declared with withExternalApiPermissions.

capabilities.name: withExternalApiPermissions
capabilities.description: Declares permissions to a Microsoft first-party or other API that is not an Aspire resource, such as Microsoft Graph.
capabilities.signature: withExternalApiPermissions(api: EntraIdWellKnownApi | EntraIdCustomApi, permissions: EntraIdExternalApiPermission[]): EntraIdApplicationResource

parameters.name: api
parameters.description: A well-known API, or an API identified by its application ID and application ID URI.

parameters.name: permissions

parameters.name: value

capabilities.name: withFederatedManagedIdentityCredential
capabilities.description: Configures a pre-existing managed identity trust for token acquisition, without provisioning or assigning an identity.
capabilities.remarks: Applies in run and publish modes. This only emits consumer configuration; it does not create federation trust.

parameters.name: managedIdentityClientId
parameters.description: The client GUID of a user-assigned managed identity that the registration already trusts.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: Optional token exchange settings.

capabilities.name: withIdTokenIssuance
capabilities.description: Enables ID-token issuance through implicit and hybrid flows for a registration created by Aspire.

capabilities.name: withInstance
capabilities.description: Configures the Entra ID instance URL. Defaults to `https://login.microsoftonline.com/`.

parameters.name: instance
parameters.description: The Entra ID instance URL, such as `https://login.microsoftonline.us/` for Azure Government or `https://contoso.ciamlogin.com/` for an external tenant.

capabilities.name: withOwners
capabilities.description: Appends an owner to both the application registration and service principal.
capabilities.remarks: Owners can manage the registration. Call repeatedly for multiple owners. Throws for existing registrations; configure their owners manually.

parameters.name: ownerObjectId
parameters.description: The directory object GUID of a user or service principal, as a literal or parameter.

capabilities.name: withPreAuthorizedApplication
capabilities.description: Pre-authorizes a client application to request some of this registration's scopes without any consent prompt.
capabilities.remarks:
Pre-authorization is separate from the client's declaration of the permission (`WithApiPermissions`)
and from consent (`WithAdminConsent`).
It lets a trusted client skip the consent prompt, which is intended for first-party clients of the same organization.
Aspire deploys each registration as its own module. Pre-authorization makes this registration wait for the client's ID, while
the client's declaration waits for this registration's ID, so two registrations cannot use both. Use a declaration with
`WithAdminConsent` on the client, or pre-authorization alone. Throws if this API registration is existing;
configure its pre-authorized clients manually. An existing client can still be pre-authorized by a registration Aspire creates.

parameters.name: client
parameters.description: The client application to pre-authorize.

parameters.name: scopeNames
parameters.description: The names of the scopes, added with `WithScope`, that the client may request.

capabilities.name: withRedirectUris
capabilities.description: Appends web redirect URIs supplied as a literal, a parameter, or an endpoint.
capabilities.signature: withRedirectUris(redirectUri: string | ParameterResource | EndpointReference, callbackPaths?: string[]): EntraIdApplicationResource

parameters.name: redirectUri
parameters.description: A full URI, a parameter containing comma-separated full URIs, or an endpoint. With callback paths, a parameter supplies a host instead.

parameters.name: callbackPaths
parameters.description: Callback paths starting with '/'. Required for an endpoint; with a host parameter, produces HTTPS URIs. Omit for full URIs.

capabilities.name: withScope
capabilities.description: Exposes a delegated permission scope that clients can request to call this registration as an API.
capabilities.remarks:
Scopes are declared explicitly. Unless an application ID URI is set with withApplicationIdUri, the registration uses api://{clientId}.
The scope's ID stays the same across deployments. Microsoft Graph does not let a deployment remove an enabled scope or change its name:
to retire a scope, deploy it with isEnabled set to false and remove it in a later deployment.
For an existing registration the scope is configuration only, which lets callers declare permissions to it. Set its id to the ID the registration defines.
capabilities.signature: withScope(name: string, description: string, options?: EntraIdScopeOptions): EntraIdApplicationResource

parameters.name: name
parameters.description: The scope's name, which appears in the token's scp claim, such as access_as_user.

parameters.name: description
parameters.description: What the scope allows, shown on the consent page.

parameters.name: options
parameters.description: Optional settings for the scope.

capabilities.name: withSendX5C
capabilities.description: Sends the `x5c` claim (the public key of the certificate) with token requests.
capabilities.remarks:
Sending `x5c` enables certificate rollover without redeploying the application. It only applies
to certificate-based credentials and increases the size of each token request, so it is opt-in.

capabilities.name: withServicePrincipalOwners
capabilities.description: Appends a service principal owner supplied as a literal directory object GUID or a parameter.
capabilities.remarks: Service principal ownership is independent of application ownership. Throws for existing registrations; configure their owners manually.

parameters.name: ownerObjectId
parameters.description: The directory object ID of a user or service principal.

capabilities.name: withSignedAssertionFile
capabilities.description: Appends a signed assertion file credential, such as an AKS workload identity token.

parameters.name: filePath
parameters.description: The token file path on the consumer. Omit to use the consumer's AZURE_FEDERATED_TOKEN_FILE setting.

capabilities.name: withSignInAudience
capabilities.description: Configures which accounts can sign in to this application.
capabilities.remarks:
The audience must match the registration's supported account types. The default uses the home tenant as TenantId.
Other audiences use organizations, common, or consumers as TenantId and also emit AppHomeTenantId.
Also configures supported account types on registrations created by Aspire. For existing registrations, configures consumers only.
Validate the tenant ID (tid) claim before allowing access to tenant-specific data.
See https://learn.microsoft.com/entra/identity-platform/claims-validation.

parameters.name: signInAudience
parameters.description: The accounts that can sign in. It must match the "Supported account types" setting of the app registration.

dtoTypes.name: EntraIdCustomApi
dtoTypes.description: Identifies an API that is not an Aspire resource by its application ID and application ID URI.

fields.name: DisplayName
fields.description: Gets a name for the API used in diagnostics and as the name of its DownstreamApis entry (its letters and digits).

fields.name: ApplicationId
fields.description: Gets the API's application (client) ID as a GUID.

fields.name: ResourceUri
fields.description: Gets the API's application ID URI, the prefix of its scopes in token requests. It is not derived from the application ID because an API can use any URI.

fields.name: BaseUrl
fields.description: Gets the API's root URL, which Aspire adds to the DownstreamApis entry as BaseUrl. When omitted, the caller must supply the address.

dtoTypes.name: EntraIdExternalApiPermission
dtoTypes.description: A permission of an API that is not an Aspire resource.

fields.name: Name
fields.description: Gets the permission's name, such as User.Read.

fields.name: Type
fields.description: Gets the kind of permission. Defaults to a delegated permission.

fields.name: Id
fields.description: Gets the permission's ID as a GUID. Required for a custom API and for a permission that a well-known API does not list by name.

dtoTypes.name: EntraIdScopeOptions
dtoTypes.description: Optional settings for a scope exposed by a created registration or described by an existing reference.

fields.name: DisplayName
fields.description: Gets the scope's title, shown on the admin consent page. Defaults to the scope's name.

fields.name: UserConsentDisplayName
fields.description: Gets the scope's title shown on the consent page for users. Defaults to the display name.

fields.name: UserConsentDescription
fields.description: Gets what the scope allows, shown on the consent page for users. Defaults to the scope's description.

fields.name: RequiresAdminConsent
fields.description: Gets whether only an administrator can consent to the scope. Defaults to false, which lets users consent.

fields.name: IsEnabled
fields.description: Gets whether clients can request the scope. Defaults to true.

fields.name: Id
fields.description: Gets the scope's ID as a GUID, which must stay the same across deployments. Aspire derives a stable ID when omitted.

dtoTypes.name: EntraIdTokenExchangeOptions
dtoTypes.description: Optional token exchange settings for a pre-existing managed identity federation trust.

fields.name: TokenExchangeUrl
fields.description: Gets the token exchange audience. Defaults to api://AzureADTokenExchange when omitted.

fields.name: TokenExchangeAuthority
fields.description: Gets the token exchange authority URL when it differs from the application's authority.

enumTypes.name: EntraIdPermissionType
enumTypes.description: The kind of permission that an application requests from an API.

memberDocs.name: Delegated
memberDocs.description: A delegated permission (an OAuth 2.0 scope). The application calls the API on behalf of a signed-in user.

memberDocs.name: Application
memberDocs.description: An application permission (an app role of the API's service principal). The application calls the API as itself, with no user.

enumTypes.name: EntraIdSignInAudience
enumTypes.description: Specifies which Microsoft accounts can sign in to an Entra ID application.
enumTypes.remarks:
The value must match the "Supported account types" setting of the app registration in the Azure portal.
The names match the `signInAudience` property of the Microsoft Graph
application resource,
which stores that setting.
Microsoft.Identity.Web reads the sign-in audience from its `TenantId` setting. A single-tenant app
uses its home tenant there. The other audiences use the keywords `organizations`, `common`,
or `consumers` instead, and pass the home tenant as `AppHomeTenantId`.

memberDocs.name: AzureADMyOrg
memberDocs.description: Only work or school accounts in the app's home tenant can sign in. This is the default.

memberDocs.name: AzureADMultipleOrgs
memberDocs.description: Work or school accounts in any Microsoft Entra tenant can sign in.

memberDocs.name: AzureADandPersonalMicrosoftAccount
memberDocs.description: Work or school accounts in any Microsoft Entra tenant, and personal Microsoft accounts, can sign in.

memberDocs.name: PersonalMicrosoftAccount
memberDocs.description: Only personal Microsoft accounts, such as Outlook.com and Xbox accounts, can sign in.
